Senses.PreferredTarget: the cypress tree in the courtyard
AlternateTargets: the juniper tree before the hall
SearchAliases: cypress tree in the courtyard case
Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one fixed case-answer; later denials and rejected explanations prevent a symbolic tree-gloss or a simple object-pointing account.

Occurrences.Kwic: 五祖師翁舉。僧問趙州。如何是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。恁麼會。便不是了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄): within Dahui Zonggao's later report, Wuzu Fayan raises Zhaozhou Congshen's historical exchange. The formula “Zhaozhou said” (州云) assigns the selected headword token to Zhaozhou; Wuzu owns the later repeated headword token and comment in the full case, while Dahui is only the outer reporter/commentator.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong's Book of Serenity (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄): Wansong Xingxiu reports a saying conventionally attributed to Zhaozhou Congshen by the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州曰), then preserves Huijue's explicit denial that his former teacher ever said it. Senses.Explanation: In these records, Zhaozhou Congshen's courtyard-cypress answer blocks both a symbolic explanation and the claim that he merely points to an external scene. It is transmitted as his answer when asked the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west and repeatedly reopened by later teachers. Dahui Zonggao reports Wuzu Fayan raising the answer and first saying that understanding it in that way is wrong, then repeating it and saying such understanding is right. Xutang Zhiyu transmits the fuller exchange: when the monastic objects that Zhaozhou should not show an external scene, Zhaozhou says he does not show an external scene and repeats the courtyard cypress. Wansong Xingxiu preserves the further transmission problem in which Huijue denies that his former teacher Zhaozhou ever said it. Ruibai Mingxue stresses that naming the cypress does not present an external scene. Tianran Hanshi warns that descendants die in the words, Hanyue Fazang rejects the explanatory imitation that makes the cypress a display of a cosmic body, and Langting Ting rebukes an answer that merely restates “the ancestral teacher's coming from the west.”
